entries.name: Bootstrap
entries.use_for: Build responsive sites quickly with a classic CSS framework and ready-made components.
entries.why: The most used CSS framework, with stable conventions, great docs and themes everywhere.
entries.summary: Classic CSS framework with a responsive grid, ready-made components and JavaScript plugins. Documented install options include npm, CDN, Composer and others.
entries.best_for: Quickly building responsive sites with familiar, well-documented components.
entries.not_for: Sites can look generic without customization; Tailwind-style utility workflows or component libraries may suit modern apps better. The README references a 6.0 alpha.

entries.name: Bootswatch
entries.use_for: Free drop-in themes for Bootstrap
entries.why: Two dozen polished Bootstrap themes as one CSS swap; the go-to way to restyle Bootstrap apps.
entries.summary: Collection of free themes for Bootstrap. Use a theme by swapping Bootstrap's stylesheet, via CDN or through Sass variable imports.
entries.best_for: Restyling a Bootstrap site with minimal effort.
entries.not_for: Bootstrap only; themes are preset looks, not a design system, and Bootstrap JavaScript is still needed for interactive components.

entries.name: Bulma
entries.use_for: Style sites with a modern, JavaScript-free CSS framework.
entries.why: Clean, readable class names and pure CSS, so it fits any JS framework.
entries.summary: Modern CSS framework based on Flexbox with readable class names and no JavaScript, installed via npm, Yarn or CDN.
entries.best_for: Styling sites with a clean pure-CSS framework in any JS stack.
entries.not_for: No built-in interactive components (dropdowns, modals need your own JS); smaller ecosystem than Bootstrap or Tailwind.

entries.name: Class Variance Authority
entries.use_for: Type-safe component variants on top of class names
entries.why: The variant API used by shadcn/ui and most Tailwind component libraries.
entries.summary: Class Variance Authority: a type-safe API for defining component class-name variants, widely used with Tailwind and shadcn/ui.
entries.best_for: Variant-based components (size, color, state) in Tailwind or CSS-class setups.
entries.not_for: Handles class strings only; does not resolve Tailwind conflicts (pair with tailwind-merge) and has no slots support.

entries.name: daisyUI
entries.use_for: Add semantic component classes and themes on top of Tailwind CSS.
entries.why: Most popular Tailwind plugin, giving btn/card-style classes and 30+ themes without JS.
entries.summary: Tailwind CSS plugin adding semantic component classes (btn, card and more) and 30+ themes without JavaScript.
entries.best_for: Faster Tailwind UI building with ready component classes and theming.
entries.not_for: Requires Tailwind CSS; CSS-only so interactive behavior is yours to implement; styling is somewhat opinionated.

entries.name: Dembrandt
entries.use_for: Extract a live website's colors, fonts, spacing and more as design tokens, and catch drift in CI.
entries.why: One command outputs W3C design tokens, and a GitHub Action compares them to a baseline.
entries.summary: A Node CLI that renders a page with Playwright, reads computed styles and returns logo, colors, typography, spacing, borders, shadows, motion, components and breakpoints. It can compare against a saved baseline and fail on drift.
entries.best_for: Reverse engineering a site's design system, or guarding a preview deploy against unplanned style changes.
entries.not_for: Cannot read canvas or WebGL sites. Dark mode needs a flag. Hover states and late-loaded content may be missed.

entries.name: Emotion
entries.use_for: Style React components with the css prop or styled API.
entries.why: Fast, flexible CSS-in-JS used under MUI and many design systems.
entries.summary: Performant, flexible CSS-in-JS library. Styles can be written as strings or objects via the css prop or styled API, with predictable composition and caching.
entries.best_for: React styling with dynamic runtime styles, or underlying MUI-style design systems.
entries.not_for: Runtime CSS-in-JS has overhead and server-component friction versus zero-runtime options like Panda or vanilla-extract.

entries.name: Less
entries.use_for: Less CSS preprocessor: variables, mixins and functions
entries.why: Still widely deployed (e.g. Ant Design theming); the other major CSS preprocessor.
entries.summary: Monorepo for Less.js, the JavaScript implementation of the Less CSS preprocessor language. The README points to lesscss.org for language, configuration and usage documentation.
entries.best_for: Projects that already use or prefer Less syntax (variables, mixins, nesting) compiled to CSS in a JavaScript toolchain.
entries.not_for: New projects that prefer Sass, PostCSS, or native CSS features; the README itself offers little usage detail.

entries.name: Linaria
entries.use_for: Write styled-components-like CSS in JS that is extracted to CSS at build time.
entries.why: Mature zero-runtime option with a familiar styled API.
entries.summary: Zero-runtime CSS-in-JS library with a styled-components-like API. Styles are extracted to CSS files at build time.
entries.best_for: CSS-in-JS ergonomics with static CSS output and no runtime cost.
entries.not_for: Needs build tooling integration (Babel/bundler plugins) and has limits on dynamic styles; development activity has varied.

entries.name: Open Props
entries.use_for: Ready-made CSS custom properties (design tokens) for colors, sizes and easing
entries.why: Framework-free design tokens for adding consistent styling to plain CSS.
entries.summary: Collection of ready-made CSS custom properties (design tokens) for colors, gradients, shadows, typography, easings, sizes and more, usable via CDN or npm with plain CSS.
entries.best_for: Adding consistent design tokens to plain CSS without a framework.
entries.not_for: Provides tokens, not components or utilities; you write the layout and component CSS yourself.

entries.name: Panda CSS
entries.use_for: Build design systems with type-safe, build-time CSS-in-JS and tokens.
entries.why: Zero-runtime, works with React Server Components, from the Chakra UI team.
entries.summary: Build-time, type-safe CSS-in-JS with design tokens, recipes and variants. Extracts styles statically and outputs modern CSS with cascade layers; works with most JS frameworks.
entries.best_for: Design systems needing zero-runtime styles that work with React Server Components.
entries.not_for: Requires a codegen and build step; the CSS-in-JS style is a bigger change than utility classes.

entries.name: PostCSS
entries.use_for: Transform CSS with JS plugins (autoprefixer, nesting, Tailwind)
entries.why: The CSS processing engine under Tailwind, Autoprefixer and most build tools.
entries.summary: Tool for transforming CSS with JavaScript plugins, such as autoprefixing, linting, nesting and future syntax. It underlies Autoprefixer, Stylelint and Tailwind.
entries.best_for: Custom CSS build pipelines and plugin-based transforms.
entries.not_for: A processing engine only; it does nothing without plugins and is not itself a styling framework.

entries.name: Sass (Dart Sass)
entries.use_for: The primary Sass/SCSS compiler, available as the sass npm package
entries.why: The reference Sass implementation; the most-used CSS preprocessor.
entries.summary: Reference implementation of Sass/SCSS, distributed as the sass npm package and as standalone binaries, with a JavaScript API and embedded compiler.
entries.best_for: Compiling Sass/SCSS in build pipelines.
entries.not_for: Sass only; the legacy JS API is deprecated, and plain CSS features may cover simpler needs.

entries.name: styled-components
entries.use_for: Write component-scoped CSS in JavaScript for React apps.
entries.why: The best-known CSS-in-JS library with theming and SSR support.
entries.summary: CSS-in-JS for React that scopes CSS to components. Works with server components, client components, streaming SSR and React Native.
entries.best_for: React apps preferring component-scoped CSS written as real CSS.
entries.not_for: Runtime styling has performance costs, and the README notes it is largely maintained by one person.

entries.name: StyleX
entries.use_for: Write co-located styles in JS that compile to atomic CSS for large apps.
entries.why: Meta styling system used on Facebook and Instagram; predictable, type-safe and scalable.
entries.summary: StyleX is a JavaScript library from Meta for defining styles for optimized user interfaces. Styles are written in JS with stylex.create and integrated through build tools; the monorepo holds the packages and examples of build-tool integrations.
entries.best_for: Large JS/React apps that want styles authored in JavaScript and compiled at build time.
entries.not_for: Projects without a JS build step, or teams wanting plain CSS or utility classes; it requires build-tool integration.

entries.name: Tailwind CSS
entries.use_for: Style any web UI with utility classes and a design-token config.
entries.why: The dominant CSS approach for new projects; fast v4 engine and the base of shadcn/ui, daisyUI and most templates.
entries.summary: Utility-first CSS framework for building custom interfaces with utility classes and a design-token configuration.
entries.best_for: New web projects wanting fast custom UI styling.
entries.not_for: Markup can become class-heavy; no ready-made components (use daisyUI or shadcn/ui). Docs live on the website, not the README.

entries.name: Tailwind Variants
entries.use_for: Tailwind-first variants API with slots, responsive variants and conflict resolution
entries.why: A richer alternative to cva, from the HeroUI team.
entries.summary: Tailwind-first variants API with slots, responsive variants, composition and built-in conflict resolution, fully typed and framework agnostic.
entries.best_for: Tailwind component libraries needing slots and responsive variants.
entries.not_for: Tailwind only; v4 no longer supports config.content.transform, which affects responsive variants.

entries.name: tailwind-merge
entries.use_for: Merge Tailwind class strings without style conflicts
entries.why: Essential utility in shadcn-style component code (the cn() helper).
entries.summary: Utility to merge Tailwind class strings in JS so later conflicting classes win (e.g. twMerge('px-2', 'p-3')).
entries.best_for: The cn() helper in Tailwind components so overrides work.
entries.not_for: Tailwind only; supports v4 (use v2.6.0 for Tailwind v3). Does not generate variants.

entries.name: UnoCSS
entries.use_for: Generate atomic CSS on demand with Tailwind-compatible or custom presets.
entries.why: Extremely fast and fully customizable engine; popular in the Vue/Vite ecosystem.
entries.summary: On-demand atomic CSS engine with presets, shortcuts and attributify mode. Fully customizable with no core utilities and about 6kb.
entries.best_for: Vite/Vue projects wanting a faster, customizable Tailwind-like engine.
entries.not_for: Smaller community and docs than Tailwind; preset-based setup requires configuration.

entries.name: vanilla-extract
entries.use_for: Write type-safe styles in TypeScript that compile to static CSS files.
entries.why: Zero runtime cost and full type safety for themes and variants; works with Vite, Next.js and others.
entries.summary: Zero-runtime stylesheets in TypeScript with locally scoped class names and CSS variables, generating static CSS at build time. Works with any framework.
entries.best_for: Type-safe themes and variants with no runtime cost.
entries.not_for: Requires bundler integration and TypeScript-file styles; less ad hoc than utility CSS.
